controls.expected: GitHub is the public product-source authority and main is the default branch.
controls.observed: The repository is public, main is the default branch, and the separate Azure Repo is empty with no default branch.

controls.expected: Repository collaboration settings preserve Azure Boards as the single backlog and remove merged branches predictably.
controls.observed: GitHub Projects is enabled and merged branches are not deleted automatically; all three merge methods are allowed.
controls.impact: A second project surface can drift from Azure Boards, and stale merged branches add avoidable repository ambiguity.
controls.correctiveAction: Disable GitHub Projects for this repository, choose the approved merge strategy, and enable merged-branch cleanup.
controls.postRemediationTest: Read repository settings through the GitHub API and confirm Projects is disabled and merged-branch deletion matches the approved strategy.

controls.expected: The main branch has an active ruleset or equivalent branch protection.
controls.observed: No active repository ruleset exists and classic protection for main is absent.
controls.impact: Direct or destructive changes can bypass the intended pull-request governance path.
controls.correctiveAction: Apply an active main ruleset with the approved pull-request, review, status-check, force-push, and deletion controls.
controls.postRemediationTest: Read back the main ruleset and verify active enforcement and exact target refs.

controls.expected: Changes to main require a pull request, one approval, stale-review dismissal, CODEOWNERS review, and resolved conversations.
controls.observed: No active branch rule enforces pull requests, reviews, CODEOWNERS approval, stale-review dismissal, or conversation resolution.
controls.impact: Repository review policy is advisory rather than mechanically enforced.
controls.correctiveAction: Configure the approved pull-request and review requirements in the active main ruleset.
controls.postRemediationTest: Read back every pull-request rule field and verify that a direct main push is rejected in the remediation validation phase.

controls.expected: Force pushes and deletion of main are blocked.
controls.observed: No active ruleset or classic protection blocks force pushes or deletion of main.
controls.impact: History or the default branch can be rewritten or removed without a protective control.
controls.correctiveAction: Add force-push and branch-deletion restrictions to the active main ruleset.
controls.postRemediationTest: Read back the rules and execute approved negative tests against a disposable branch pattern before testing main protection.

controls.expected: The repository validation workflow is a required status check for main.
controls.observed: The validation workflow exists and has successful main runs, but no branch rule requires its check.
controls.impact: A change can merge without repository validation succeeding.
controls.correctiveAction: Require the exact repository validation check name in the active main ruleset.
controls.postRemediationTest: Read back required checks and prove an intentionally failing pull request cannot merge.

controls.expected: CODEOWNERS is present and parses without errors.
controls.observed: CODEOWNERS is present and the GitHub API reports no parsing errors.

controls.expected: GitHub Actions uses read-only default token permissions.
controls.observed: The default workflow token permission is read; workflows cannot approve pull requests through the default token.

controls.expected: Tracked GitHub Actions are pinned to reviewed immutable revisions.
controls.observed: The action-pin manifest and tracked workflow contracts pass in the 248-test repository suite.

controls.expected: A successful repository validation record exists on current main.
controls.observed: A completed successful validation run has a head SHA equal to current main; 19 of the last 20 recorded main runs succeeded.

controls.expected: Dependency updates and available repository security analysis are enabled to the approved baseline.
controls.observed: Secret scanning and push protection are enabled, but Dependabot security updates and several optional secret-analysis capabilities are disabled.
controls.impact: Known vulnerable dependency updates may not be raised automatically even though weekly action updates are configured.
controls.correctiveAction: Enable Dependabot security updates and record an explicit decision for optional secret-analysis capabilities.
controls.postRemediationTest: Read back security-and-analysis state and confirm a successful Dependabot security-update configuration.

controls.expected: The Azure Boards GitHub App is valid and scoped to the approved repository.
controls.observed: Azure DevOps reports one valid installation-token connection bound to the expected GitHub repository.

controls.expected: Administrative access and ruleset bypass actors are explicitly bounded and reviewed.
controls.observed: One direct collaborator is visible, but no active ruleset exists and effective administrator or bypass scope was not published in the sanitized evidence.
controls.postRemediationTest: Export the sanitized administrator boundary, configure only approved pull-request bypass actors, and read back every ruleset bypass actor and mode.

controls.expected: GitHub environments referenced by bootstrap or governance workflows exist with the approved protection rules.
controls.observed: Only the Copilot environment exists and it has no protection rules; the reviewed Tenant 1 bootstrap environment is absent.
controls.impact: Bootstrap workflows cannot rely on a reviewed environment boundary or required approval before privileged tenant operations.
controls.correctiveAction: Create the reviewed Tenant 1 bootstrap environment, restrict branches, add the approved protection rules, and keep deployment gates in Azure DevOps.
controls.postRemediationTest: Read back the environment, branch policy, variables, protection rules, reviewer settings, and self-review behavior.

controls.expected: The Tenant 1 Azure DevOps project is private and well formed.
controls.observed: The expected project is present, private, and reports a well-formed state.

controls.expected: The project process supports the intended Epic, Feature, User Story, Task, and Bug hierarchy.
controls.observed: The project uses the Basic process, but the required backlog hierarchy remains Proposed Baseline and has not been approved for comparison.
controls.postRemediationTest: Read back process metadata and create a synthetic work-item hierarchy in the remediation validation phase.

controls.expected: Teams, area paths, and dated iterations represent the HR delivery model.
controls.observed: One default team uses the normal project-root area and Sprint 1 has no dates; no approved team or sprint-cadence target exists for comparison.
controls.postRemediationTest: Read back teams, team fields, areas, iterations, dates, and default backlog settings.

controls.expected: The project has a valid GitHub App connection.
controls.observed: One valid GitHub connection uses an installation token, consistent with GitHub App authentication.

controls.expected: The GitHub connection is bound to exactly the approved repository.
controls.observed: The connection contains exactly one repository and it is the approved GitHub source repository.

controls.expected: Tenant 1 uses one GitHub repository connected to one Azure DevOps organization and project.
controls.observed: The live connection matches the approved Tenant 1 repository and project, consistent with the platform one-connection constraint.

controls.expected: An existing AB# transaction proves GitHub-to-Boards linkage and intended state transition behavior.
controls.observed: No work item currently has an external GitHub link, so the configured connection has no runtime traceability proof.
controls.postRemediationTest: Create an approved synthetic work item, reference it from a branch, commit, and pull request, merge to main, and verify links and the intended state transition.

controls.expected: Every Azure Repo has an explicit narrow role and does not compete with GitHub product source.
controls.observed: The auto-created Azure Repo is empty with no default branch, but it retains the project name and has not been renamed or formally assigned the proposed configuration/template role.
controls.impact: The empty repository does not duplicate source today, but its name and unresolved purpose create contributor and automation ambiguity.
controls.correctiveAction: Approve whether to rename and repurpose the empty repository for tenant-private configuration or remove it; document the one-way content boundary.
controls.postRemediationTest: Read back repository name, size, default branch, permissions, and documented purpose, and confirm no product source exists there.

controls.expected: Project groups and effective permissions implement least privilege and separation of duties.
controls.observed: Expected built-in groups and dedicated endpoint and release administrator groups exist, but unrestricted membership and effective permission expansion were intentionally not collected.
controls.postRemediationTest: Export the Azure DevOps detailed permission report, sanitize identities, and verify effective permissions and group memberships against an approved role matrix.

controls.expected: HR solution CI/CD pipeline definitions exist.
controls.observed: The Azure DevOps project has no pipeline definitions.
controls.impact: No Azure Pipelines delivery path exists for the HR solution.
controls.correctiveAction: Create reviewed YAML pipelines for HR solution CI and gated promotion from GitHub source.
controls.postRemediationTest: Read back pipeline definitions and verify their repository, YAML paths, triggers, permissions, and disabled-manual-bypass controls.

controls.expected: Every HR pipeline uses a separate Azure Pipelines GitHub App connection restricted to the approved repository and checks out that source directly.
controls.observed: No Azure Pipeline or separate Azure Pipelines GitHub connection exists; the working Azure Boards GitHub App does not provide pipeline repository authentication or triggers.
controls.impact: Future pipeline authors could accidentally use the empty Azure Repo or another source unless the GitHub source contract is explicit.
controls.correctiveAction: Configure the Azure Pipelines GitHub App for only the approved repository, bind pipeline and YAML paths to it, and declare immutable source-ref behavior.
controls.postRemediationTest: Read back the pipeline GitHub connection and repository authorization, then verify trigger delivery, GitHub Checks publication, and checked-out commit SHA.

controls.expected: CI and pull-request triggers are scoped to the approved branches and paths.
controls.observed: No pipeline trigger configuration exists.
controls.impact: The HR solution has no repeatable validation trigger and future trigger behavior is undefined.
controls.correctiveAction: Define pull-request and main CI triggers with solution and pipeline path filters.
controls.postRemediationTest: Open an approved synthetic pull request that changes an HR solution path and verify exactly the intended CI run starts.

controls.expected: CI validates, exports or synchronizes, unpacks, checks, and builds the HR solution.
controls.observed: No Azure Pipeline or run proves HR solution validation or build.
controls.impact: The unmanaged DEV solution cannot be converted into a reviewable, reproducible release artifact.
controls.correctiveAction: Implement the approved Power Platform Build Tools CI sequence and source-drift checks.
controls.postRemediationTest: Run CI on an approved commit and verify solution validation, unpack comparison, checker results, and managed build output.

controls.expected: One immutable managed artifact is produced once and promoted unchanged.
controls.observed: No pipeline run or artifact exists.
controls.impact: TEST and PROD cannot be proven to receive the same reviewed solution artifact.
controls.correctiveAction: Publish a versioned managed solution artifact with provenance and consume that exact artifact in deployment stages.
controls.postRemediationTest: Compare artifact identity and hash across CI, TEST deployment, and PROD deployment records.

controls.expected: The deployment path builds one managed artifact from the unmanaged DEV source and promotes that unchanged artifact to TEST and PROD.
controls.observed: No deployment stages or releases exist; the unmanaged HR solution is present only in DEV.
controls.impact: The solution has no controlled path to TEST or PROD.
controls.correctiveAction: Implement deployment stages that import the managed artifact into TEST and PROD with stage-specific settings.
controls.postRemediationTest: Run an approved release and verify the same managed version in TEST and PROD with recorded import results.

controls.expected: Azure DevOps deployment environments represent TEST and PROD release boundaries.
controls.observed: The Azure DevOps project has no deployment environments.
controls.impact: There is no resource boundary on which to enforce deployment permissions, history, approvals, or checks.
controls.correctiveAction: Create reviewed TEST and PROD Azure DevOps environments with restricted pipeline authorization.
controls.postRemediationTest: Read back environment metadata, permissions, authorized pipelines, and deployment history.

controls.expected: TEST and PROD use resource-administered approvals and checks outside YAML.
controls.observed: There are no environments or checks; the checks list cannot be meaningfully evaluated without a resource.
controls.impact: A future YAML author could control deployment flow without an independently administered gate.
controls.correctiveAction: Configure required approvals and checks on the protected environments or service connections, with PROD approvers separate from pipeline authors.
controls.postRemediationTest: Read check configurations and execute an approved release that pauses until the expected approver acts.

controls.expected: Ready, non-personal, least-privilege service connections exist for required targets.
controls.observed: The Azure DevOps project has no service connections.
controls.impact: Azure Pipelines cannot authenticate to Azure or Power Platform targets.
controls.correctiveAction: Create stage-specific, non-personal service connections using the safest supported authentication scheme and minimum scope.
controls.postRemediationTest: Read endpoint type, readiness, authorization scheme, scope, project references, and pipeline authorization without retrieving secrets.

controls.expected: Workload identity is used where the supported task and service-connection type permit it.
controls.observed: No service connection exists, so authentication scheme compatibility cannot be evaluated.
controls.postRemediationTest: Read back each connection scheme and compare it with current Microsoft support for the exact Azure and Power Platform task types.

controls.expected: Tenant-specific values and sensitive material use governed variable groups or secure resources rather than public or inline values.
controls.observed: No variable group or secure file exists, while tenant-specific identifiers and endpoints are currently committed in the public repository.
controls.impact: A future pipeline has no governed configuration source, and current public configuration conflicts with the documented tenant boundary.
controls.correctiveAction: Define the tenant-private configuration store, classify each value, and connect only reviewed non-secret and secret resources to authorized pipelines.
controls.postRemediationTest: Scan the public repository and read Azure DevOps resource metadata to confirm the approved public/private split.

controls.expected: Agent pool access and parallel-job entitlement can execute the HR pipeline.
controls.observed: The Microsoft-hosted pool is visible, but no pipeline run exists and parallel-job entitlement was not available through the collected API surface.
controls.postRemediationTest: Queue an approved validation run after pipeline creation and confirm it acquires an agent without a parallelism error.

controls.expected: Build-service and protected-resource permissions implement least privilege.
controls.observed: Build and release groups exist, but no pipeline, service connection, environment, or resource authorization exists to evaluate effective delivery permissions.
controls.postRemediationTest: Export sanitized effective permissions for build identities and protected resources after they exist, and compare them with the approved role matrix.

controls.expected: A required-template check enforces governed deployment structure from a tenant-private template source outside pipeline-author control.
controls.observed: No pipeline, governed template repository role, protected resource, or required-template check exists.
controls.impact: Future pipeline authors could remove required deployment structure or controls in YAML without an independently administered template gate.
controls.correctiveAction: Approve the tenant-private template location, create the governed template, and attach a required-template check to a protected resource outside pipeline-author control.
controls.postRemediationTest: Read back the required-template check and prove a pipeline that omits the governed template cannot consume the protected resource.

controls.expected: A dedicated non-personal Entra application and service principal back the delivery identity.
controls.observed: No application matched the reviewed delivery-identity name, and no Azure DevOps service connection identifies a delivery principal; no delivery identity is evidenced as configured for pipeline use.
controls.impact: The delivery platform has no non-personal identity for Azure or Power Platform automation.
controls.correctiveAction: Create and approve a dedicated delivery application and service principal with a documented lifecycle and owners.
controls.postRemediationTest: Read back application, service principal, ownership, credentials or federation, and exact service-connection references.

controls.expected: Federated credentials exactly match workload-identity service connections where supported.
controls.observed: No delivery application or service connection exists, so no federated subject can be validated.
controls.postRemediationTest: Compare each federated credential issuer, subject, and audience with the exact service connection read-back.

controls.expected: Azure role assignments use least privilege and minimum scope.
controls.observed: No delivery service principal exists, so its Azure role assignments cannot be evaluated.
controls.postRemediationTest: List role assignments for the delivery principal and reject standing Owner, User Access Administrator, or unsupported broad Contributor scope.

controls.expected: Distinct DEV, TEST, and PROD Power Platform environments exist with the intended lifecycle roles.
controls.observed: DEV and TEST are reachable Sandbox environments and PROD is a reachable Production environment. This PASS is limited to existence, reachability, and lifecycle type; access boundaries and data-policy coverage were not assessed.

controls.expected: The delivery application user exists, is enabled, and has approved roles in each required environment.
controls.observed: Environment application-user inventories are readable, but no approved delivery application exists to identify the required application-user record or roles.
controls.postRemediationTest: Query each environment for the exact delivery application ID and verify enabled state, business unit, and least-privilege security roles.

controls.expected: The reviewed HR solution and custom publisher prerequisites exist in DEV.
controls.observed: DEV contains unmanaged HR solution version 0.0.0.1 with the reviewed custom publisher and prefix.

controls.expected: Tenant-specific identifiers, administrator identities, subscription IDs, and environment endpoints remain outside the public repository.
controls.observed: The public repository contains tenant, subscription, project, environment, and administrator identifiers in committed manifests and evidence.
controls.impact: Tenant cloning can propagate the wrong identifiers, and the committed configuration contradicts the documented tenant-private boundary.
controls.correctiveAction: Approve an explicit public/private classification, move tenant-private values to the tenant-bound configuration repository or governed resources, and retain only safe aliases and schemas publicly.
controls.postRemediationTest: Run a repository-wide forbidden-data scan and compare public manifests with the approved allowlist.

controls.expected: An existing GitHub commit or pull request links to an Azure Boards work item.
controls.observed: No Azure Boards work item has an external GitHub link.
controls.postRemediationTest: Execute the approved AB# synthetic transaction defined for ADO-007.

controls.expected: An existing Azure Pipeline run links source and work items.
controls.observed: No Azure Pipeline or run exists.
controls.postRemediationTest: Run CI for a commit linked to an approved work item and verify source and Integrated in build links.

controls.expected: An existing runtime record proves artifact identity and gated environment deployment.
controls.observed: No pipeline run, artifact, Azure DevOps environment, approval, or deployment record exists.
controls.postRemediationTest: Execute an approved end-to-end release and correlate commit, work item, artifact hash, approvals, imports, and final solution version.

controls.expected: Tenant 1 setup is declarative, parameterized, and read-back validated.
controls.observed: Repository manifests, discovery scripts, workflows, and tests exist, but Boards configuration, delivery identities, service connections, pipelines, and deployment environments are not represented as completed desired state.
controls.impact: Tenant 1 cannot yet be rebuilt end to end from the repository, and manual configuration can drift.
controls.correctiveAction: Extend the desired-state and conformance model to Boards, pipelines, identities, connections, environments, and post-deployment evidence.
controls.postRemediationTest: Rebuild or dry-run the Tenant 1 control plane from reviewed parameters and compare every supported read-back with desired state.

controls.expected: Tenant 2 and Tenant 3 can seed independent repositories without inheriting Tenant 1 identifiers or another tenant configuration.
controls.observed: The repository contains multiple tenant manifests and evidence, while the per-tenant topology and removal/backport runbook remain Proposed Baseline or work in progress.
controls.impact: A repository clone can retain another tenant owner, identifiers, endpoints, or discovery evidence and can connect to only one Azure Boards organization.
controls.correctiveAction: Approve the per-tenant topology, finish the seed-and-sanitize runbook, and add an automated tenant-isolation conformance test.
controls.postRemediationTest: Create a disposable clone from the runbook and prove it contains exactly one tenant manifest, no foreign identifiers, and one intended Boards connection target.

controls.expected: The one-repository-to-one-Azure-DevOps-project North Star and source/configuration boundaries are formally approved and internally consistent.
controls.observed: ADR-0001, ADR-0002, ADR-0012, and the Tenant 1 single-source design remain Proposed Baseline, with unresolved differences about Azure Repo purpose and tenant-private configuration.
controls.impact: Administrators cannot configure a durable target safely while the authoritative topology, private-configuration location, and Azure Repo role remain unapproved.
controls.correctiveAction: Run an attended decision review, reconcile the ADR set, approve one target topology, and supersede conflicting text.
controls.postRemediationTest: Verify the ADR catalogue has one approved, internally consistent decision and that runbooks, manifests, and remediation tasks reference it.
